public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 40

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α] (G : SimpleGraph α)

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 40](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a nontrivial connected graph `G` the size `f(G)` of a largest induced forest
satisfies `f(G) ≥ ceil((p(G) + b(G) + 1)/2)` where `p(G)` is the path cover
number and `b(G)` is the largest induced bipartite subgraph size.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture40 (h_conn : G.Connected) (h_nontrivial : 1 < Fintype.card α) :
    ⌈(((pathCoverNumber G : ℝ) + b G + 1) / 2)⌉ ≤  G.largestInducedForestSize := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40

reformulations.difference: The source defines p(G) as 'the minimum number of vertex disjoint paths needed to cover the vertices of the graph'. The Lean `pathCoverNumber` is the sInf of `P.card` over families `P : Finset (Finset α)` of pairwise-disjoint vertex sets covering `univ`, each equal to `p.support.toFinset` for some G-walk `p` with `p.IsPath`. So a path cover is recorded by its vertex sets, not by the paths. The source's 'more than one vertex' is stated twice, as `[Nontrivial α]` and as `1 < Fintype.card α`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A set of k vertex-disjoint paths covering V gives k distinct, nonempty, pairwise-disjoint supports covering univ, so P has card k. Conversely, each s in such a P is the vertex set of a G-path; choosing one path per s gives |P| vertex-disjoint paths covering V. So the two minima agree. The empty set cannot be in P because supports are nonempty, so the count cannot be padded. The feasible set is nonempty (the singleton partition), so the sInf is a genuine minimum, and it is at least 1 for nonempty α. The two nontriviality hypotheses are both equivalent to 'more than one vertex'. Int.ceil x ≤ (n:ℤ) iff x ≤ n, matching CEIL. Checked in Lean on the tight case K_{1,3}: pathCoverNumber = 2, largestInducedForestSize = 4, b = 4 (no sorry), and the inequality holds with equality.

review.notes: No problems found. The source host cms.dt.uh.edu / cms.uhd.edu is unreachable over HTTPS from the sandbox, so I read Wayback Machine snapshots through the Google Translate proxy (web-archive-org.translate.goog). WOWII all.html (2026-07-26 snapshot) gives Conjecture 40 as: 'O 40. If G is a simple connected graph on more than one vertex, then f(G) ≥ CEIL[(p(G)+b(G)+1)/2]', with definitions p = path covering number, b = bipartite number, f = forest number. DeLaVina's remark there says the case p(G) = 1 follows from f ≥ b/2 + 1; the general case is open. The 2008 open.html has the same wording, and #40 is missing from the 2026 resolved list. The Lean statement elaborates to `⌈(↑G.pathCoverNumber + G.b + 1) / 2⌉ ≤ ↑G.largestInducedForestSize` in ℤ, for finite connected G with more than one vertex. This is exactly the source claim. Lean checks on the star K_{1,3} (no sorry): pathCoverNumber = 2, largestInducedForestSize = 4, b = 4, and the inequality is tight. A separate C brute force of the conjecture found no violation among all labeled connected graphs on 2 to 7 vertices (counts match OEIS A001187) or among 14,677 random connected graphs on 8 to 13 vertices, consistent with 'research open'. arXiv searches found 2026 papers settling other Graffiti.pc/WOWII conjectures, but none about #40. I deliberately did not read the GitHub repo cozuya/wowii-conjecture-40, because it contains files about formal-conjectures pull requests. Cosmetic only: the two nontriviality hypotheses are redundant, and the theorem docstring does not use LaTeX.
